title: Multi-tenant emergency model remediation: orchestrated feature-gate evacuation and hotpatch sequencing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: A subset of canaries in the hosted plane began returning hallucinated attribution metadata after rollout of model v2026-03-beta. Multiple enterprise tenants on Dedicated reported increased error rates and quality SLO violations. This ticket defines an orchestrated remediation that: (1) evacuates traffic from the new feature gate and model slice, (2) applies a targeted live hotpatch to the runtime serialization code path, (3) reconciles KV-cache divergence for tenant slices, and (4) coordinates customer comms and SLA-sensitive rollback handoffs across Hosted/Dedicated/Private environments.

Goals: 
- Halt customer-facing degradation within 15 minutes for affected tenants.
- Restore quality SLOs to pre-rollout baseline for all slices within 4 hours.
- Ensure no long-lived KV-cache inconsistency after rollback or hotpatch.

Scope & constraints: 
- Affected planes: hosted (api.redwood.ai), dedicated pools (us-west-dedicated-03), and a small number of private deployments on 1.24.
- Must preserve tenant data residency guarantees during evacuation.
- For Private customers without push access, coordinate through Solutions/Customer Success for hotpatch deployment windows.

Immediate mitigation plan (ordered):
1) Feature-gate evacuation (Evacuation Fence): flip the rollout feature-gate flag for the flagged model slices to OFF. This triggers traffic routing override and moves CANARY traffic to the previous stable model variant. Command (admin console): PATCH /v1/admin/rollouts/{rollout_id}/evacuate {action: "evacuate"}.
2) Routing-policy override: apply emergency routing policy in global routing rules to direct affected tenant shards to fallback host pools using route override token: EVAC-<timestamp>.
3) Sync KV-cache tombstone pass: run kv-repair --slice=<slice_id> --mode=two-phase to reconcile stale KV state between rolling variant caches. This prevents stale prompts/responses when traffic flips back.
4) Apply hotpatch: if the evacuation does not fully restore baseline, do a live-apply hotpatch to runtime serialization (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2197). Hotpatch plan uses the live-patch-controller CanaryWave=1 then 2, with TTL backstop of 60 minutes.
5) Canary revalidation: run synthetic slice-level canaries (synthetic traffic from canary-runner) with the pre-rollout prompt set (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/QA/Canary+Prompt+Sets) and validate token-level distributions and hallucination metrics.
6) Customer comms & SLA: inform impacted customers via the incident channel and schedule dedicated post-mortems. Use template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Customer+Escalation+Template.

Validation & success criteria: 
- Metric checks (Datadog dashboards): hallucination_rate_slice < 0.5% and latency_p50 < 180ms for affected tenants for 30m rolling window.
- KV-cache reconciliation sanity: no >1% addressable cache-miss spike after traffic flip.
- No new 5xx error rate spikes during live-patch window.

Rollback & fallforward choreography: 
- Rolling rollback: if hotpatch introduces regressions, invoke rollback API: POST /v1/admin/rollouts/{rollout_id}/rollback with param target_variant=stable. This triggers a coordinated rollback across hosted/dedicated/private via crossplane handshake.
- Tenant-slice pinning: for sensitive tenants, pin them to the previous model via tenant config: PUT /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/model_pin {model: "stable-2026-02"}.
- Post-rollback cache rehydration: run kv-rehydrate --tenant={tenant_id} to restore consistent KV state after rollback.

Operational roles & escalation path: 
- Incident Lead: Aisha Patel (owner of this ticket)
- Runtime Lead: Jonas Meyer (assignee)
- SRE/Networking: Miguel Santos (oncall)
- Solutions/Success Liaison: Priya Shah (customer contact)
- Exec comms (if >5 enterprise customers affected): notify CTO and Head of Support.

Observability playbook (what to watch): 
- Datadog queries: 
  - canary.hallucination_rate.by_slice
  - model.latency.p50/p95.by_tenant
  - runtime.kvcache.staleness.by_slice
  - rollout.error_rate.by_rollout_id
- Synthetic checks: canary-runner/job/{rollout_id} logs and artifacts in GCS: gs://redwood-canary-artifacts/{rollout_id}/.

Communication templates (customer-facing snippet): 
- Initial ack: "We’ve identified a regression in the recent model rollout impacting your tenant slice. We’ve initiated an emergency rollback/evacuation and will provide updates every 15 minutes. Owner: Aisha Patel."
- Post-resolution: attach timeline, remediation steps taken, and preventative actions.

Follow-ups & permanent mitigations (postmortem action items): 
- Add a feature-gate dry-run verifier in the console to estimate KV-change impact before rollout.
- Instrument rollout controller to record per-slice KV-change diffs and expose preflight warnings.
- Automate evacuation fencing with a single-button immediate-evac + cache-repair orchestration.

Artifacts & links: 
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2197
- Canary prompts & eval suite: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/QA/Canary+Prompt+Sets
- Customer escalation template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Customer+Escalation+Template
- Runbooks: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Live+Hotpatch+Runbook
